feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (score 482.7) is the only raced evidence: oval 20/20 finished at 1.69 s mean, s-bend 5/20, slalom 0/20, with max_error of 0.060 to 0.064 m on the failed runs and rms_error of 0.023 to 0.030 m. So the limit is peak excursion on bends, not average tracking. This package keeps the proposed +/-0.075 m span, 16 mm footprint and sensors at y = 0.07 m, and takes the 0.10 m track and 0.5 kg mass as proposed. Keeping the outer weights at +/-1.5 keeps the signal scale tested in iteration 1 on a wider span. kp is lowered to 1.4 to offset the higher yaw gain from the narrower track. Integration answers: the 16 mm footprint and 0.5 kg mass effects on oscillation can only be read from the next race's steering_oscillation (iteration 1 oval: 0.299; s-bend: 0.338). Iteration 1 showed no clear forward-lead lag, since the 0.06 m lead gave no oscillation spike. Next race: if max_error on the slalom is still above 0.06 m with line_loss_events of 1 or more, the span and sensing are probably not the only limit, so try reducing the outer weights to +/-1.0 to lower steering gain at the edges. If steering_oscillation on the oval rises above about 0.35 while max_error is under 0.06 m, the narrower track is too aggressive: restore wheel_track to 0.12 m. Change one field at a time so the effect can be attributed.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35 on the oval while max_error is under 0.06 m: restore wheel_track from 0.10 m to 0.12 m. Evidence: iteration 1 oval steering_oscillation was 0.299 at 0.12 m track and 0.6 kg mass, so the narrower track plus lighter mass may add jitter.

If slalom line_loss_events stay at 1.0 or above with max_error above 0.06 m: keep the +/-0.075 m span but reduce the outer sensor weights from +/-1.5 to +/-1.0 with the inner weights scaled to match, to limit edge steering gain. Evidence: iteration 1 slalom had 1.0 line-loss events and max_error 0.064 m at +/-0.06 m span.

If the next race is clean on the s-bend (completion above 50 percent) but the slalom still fails: try a 12 mm footprint (sensor_size 0.012) to sharpen edge readings. Evidence: iteration 0 with 12 mm footprint and 6 cm span was worse on all tracks, so test this only with the wider span already in place.
